task_context.reference_solution:
From the angle addition formula,
\[1 = \tan 45^\circ = \tan (20^\circ + 25^\circ) = \frac{\tan 20^\circ + \tan 25^\circ}{1 - \tan 20^\circ \tan 25^\circ},\]so $\tan 20^\circ + \tan 25^\circ = 1 - \tan 20^\circ \tan 25^\circ.$

Then
\[(1 + \tan 20^\circ)(1 + \tan 25^\circ) = 1 + \tan 20^\circ + \tan 25^\circ + \tan 20^\circ \tan 25^\circ = \boxed{2}.\]

If you set $A=20^\circ$ and $B=25^\circ$, you know the result is 1. Try rearranging that equation to express the sum $\tan 20^\circ + \tan 25^\circ$ in terms of their product.

If I replace the sum with $1 - \tan 20 \tan 25$, I get $1 + (1 - \tan 20 \tan 25) + \tan 20 \tan 25$, which simplifies to 2. Is that correct?
